title: Eleven Rules in the Lock-up
sub: D.K. Basu v State of W.B. (1997) · Arnesh Kumar (2014)
scene: a night-time Indian police lock-up seen through iron bars, a plain-clothes officer writing an arrest memo on a clipboard while a worried young man sits on a bench, a wall clock showing midnight, a witness signing the memo; cool blue and amber light

title: The Right to Stay Silent
scene: a dignified middle-aged Indian woman politician in a cotton saree seated across a table from an investigating officer, a written questionnaire between them, her lips closed and hand raised in polite refusal, a portrait of Gandhi and a ceiling fan behind; realistic digital painting

title: The Midnight Search
sub: Pooran Mal v Director of Inspection (1974)
scene: income-tax officers with torches searching a wealthy merchant's old haveli at midnight, opening steel almirahs and pulling out ledgers and gold, the merchant in a dhoti watching anxiously from a doorway; dramatic torchlight in a dark room

title: The Chief Minister's Complaint
sub: State of Haryana v Bhajan Lal (1992)
scene: a stern Indian High Court courtroom, a judge in black robe tearing a page of an FIR in half as a symbolic gesture, a politician in white kurta watching from the dock, marble pillars and the scales of justice

title: Bail, Not Jail
sub: Gurbaksh Singh Sibbia v State of Punjab (1980)
scene: a Sikh man in a turban walking out through the open gate of an Indian jail into morning sunlight, a lawyer holding a bail order beside him, jail walls and a guard in the background; hopeful golden light

title: Shah Bano's Twenty-Five Rupees
sub: Mohd. Ahmed Khan v Shah Bano Begum (1985)
scene: an elderly Muslim woman in a white saree and headscarf standing alone on the steps of a colonial-era Indian court building holding a single folded court order, pigeons on the steps, soft morning light; dignified realistic painting

title: The Last Jury
sub: K.M. Nanavati v State of Maharashtra (1962)
scene: a 1959 Bombay sessions courtroom with a twelve-man jury in the box, a handsome naval officer in white uniform standing in the dock, the judge in a wig looking sternly at the jury, black-and-white newspaper headlines pinned on the wall; vintage sepia-toned realistic painting

title: Tried Twice?
sub: Maqbool Hussain v State of Bombay (1953)
scene: a man in a 1950s suit at a customs counter of an old Bombay airport, a customs officer holding up a confiscated gold bar, and behind them the same man standing in a criminal court dock — two scenes split by a vertical line; realistic painting

title: Rarest of the Rare
sub: Bachan Singh v State of Punjab (1980)
scene: a grey stone High Court bench with three judges in black robes, a red-bound death sentence file open on the desk, a scale of justice tipping in the foreground, a distant hangman's noose faintly visible in a shadowed corridor; solemn, muted tones

title: The Boy Who Was Not Tried as a Man
sub: Nirbhaya juvenile · Pratap Singh v State of Jharkhand (2005)
scene: a teenage boy in a plain shirt sitting alone on a bench in a Juvenile Justice Board room with soft yellow walls and children's drawings, a woman social worker and a magistrate without robes at a round table, candles of a Delhi protest march glowing through a window; gentle but serious tone

title: A Second Chance
sub: Ramji Missar v State of Bihar (1963) · Probation of Offenders Act 1958
scene: a young first-time offender shaking hands with a probation officer outside a district court, his mother watching with relief, a bond paper in his other hand, a village road and morning sun behind; warm hopeful colours
